text: and fruits such as they desire this is meant to point out that eating and drinking in Paradise is done according to their desires in contrast to the case in this world where it is predominantly determined by what people are able to procure. It will also be said to them

arabic: كُلُواْ وَٱشْرَبُواْ هَنِيـۤئاً بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
text: ‘Eat and drink in full enjoyment hanī’an is a circumstantial qualifier in other words mutahanni’īna for what you used to do’ in the way of obedience.

arabic: إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text: Indeed so in the same way that We reward the God-fearing do We reward the virtuous.

arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
text: Woe to the deniers on that day!

arabic: كُلُواْ وَتَمَتَّعُواْ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ مُّجْرِمُونَ
text: ‘Eat and enjoy — addressing the disbelievers in this world — for a little time at the end of which comes death — this is meant as a threat for them. Indeed you are guilty!’

arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
text: Woe to the deniers on that day!

arabic: وَإذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱرْكَعُواْ لاَ يَرْكَعُونَ
text: For when it is said to them ‘Bow down!’ perform prayer they do not bow down they do not perform prayer.

arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
text: Woe to the deniers on that day!

arabic: فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ
text: In what discourse then after this namely the Qur’ān will they believe? In other words they cannot believe in any other of God’s Scriptures after having denied this Qur’ān since it comprises that inimitability i‘jāz which none of the others do.

arabic: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
text: About what about what thing are they the people of Quraysh questioning one another?

arabic: عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text: About the awesome tiding this is the explication of that ‘thing’; the interrogative is meant to emphasise its magnitude — this awesome tiding is the Qur’ān comprising news of the Resurrection and so on which the Prophet s brought —

arabic: ٱلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ
text: concerning which they are at variance for the believers affirm it while the disbelievers repudiate it.

arabic: كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ
text: No indeed! — a disavowal — they will come to know what will befall them for their rejection of it.

arabic: ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ
text: Again no indeed! They will come to know! reiterated for emphasis; thumma is added here to declare that the second threat of chastisement is more severe than the first. God exalted be He then alludes to His power to resurrect saying

arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلأَرْضَ مِهَٰداً
text: Have We not made the earth a cradle a bed like a cradle

arabic: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَاداً
text: and the mountains pegs? with which the earth is tied down like tents are tied down with pegs the interrogative is meant as an affirmative.

arabic: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً
text: And created you in pairs? males and females

arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتاً
text: and made your sleep for rest? repose for your bodies

arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيلَ لِبَاساً
text: and made the night a cloak? to cover you with its darkness

arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشاً
text: and made the day for livelihood? a time for seeking livelihood

arabic: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعاً شِدَاداً
text: and built above you seven mighty ones? seven heavens shidād is the plural of shadīda that is to say strong and sturdy unaffected by the passage of time

arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجاً وَهَّاجاً
text: and set a radiant lamp? namely the sun

arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَآءً ثَجَّاجاً
text: and sent down from the rain-clouds mu‘sirāt the clouds due to give rain similar to the term mu‘sir which denotes a girl nearing menstruation cascading water? pouring forth

arabic: لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبّاً وَنَبَاتاً
text: that with it We may bring forth grains such as wheat and plants such as figs

arabic: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافاً
text: and gardens orchards of intertwining foliage? alfāf is the plural of lafīf similar in pattern to sharīf ‘noble’ plural ashrāf.

arabic: إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتاً
text: Verily the Day of Decision for creatures is the tryst a time fixed for reward and punishment

arabic: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجاً
text: the day the Trumpet the Horn is blown yawma yunfakhu fī’l-sūri is either a substitution for or an explication of yawma’l-fasli ‘the Day of Decision’ the blower being Isrāfīl and you come forth from your graves to the site of the Resurrection in droves in diverse groups

arabic: وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَاباً
text: and the heaven is opened read futtihat or futihat sundered for the descent of the angels and becomes as gates it becomes a heaven with gates

arabic: وَسُيِّرَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَاباً
text: and the mountains are set in motion dislocated from their positions and become as a mirage as fine dust that is to say like it in terms of its levity when in motion.

arabic: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَاداً
text: Verily Hell lurks in ambush mirsādan in the sense of rāsidatan or mursidatan ‘lying in wait’

arabic: لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآباً
text: for the rebellious the disbelievers who will not be able to avoid it it is a resort a retreat for them and so they will enter it

arabic: لاَّبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَاباً
text: to remain lābithīna is an implied circumstantial qualifier in other words their remaining therein will be decreed to be therein for ages for endless epochs ahqāb is the plural of huqb

arabic: لاَّ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْداً وَلاَ شَرَاباً
text: tasting in it neither coolness neither sleep something which they will not taste therein nor drink nor anything that is imbibed for the sake of its delightful taste

arabic: إِلاَّ حَمِيماً وَغَسَّاقاً
text: except boiling water of extreme temperatures and pus read ghasāqan or ghassāqan which is the vile matter that is emitted by the bodies of the inhabitants of the Fire which is what they will indeed taste. They are given this pair of tortures

arabic: جَزَآءً وِفَاقاً
text: as a fitting requital one that accords with the nature of their deeds for there is no sin greater than disbelief and no chastisement greater than the Fire.

arabic: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ لاَ يَرْجُونَ حِسَاباً
text: Indeed they never feared any reckoning given their rejection of the Resurrection

arabic: وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّاباً
text: and they denied Our signs the Qur’ān mendaciously

arabic: وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَاباً
text: and everything in the way of deeds have We kept count of have We recorded precisely in a Book as individual written records in the Preserved Tablet in order to requite creatures in accordance with them including the record of their denial of the Qur’ān.

arabic: فَذُوقُواْ فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ إِلاَّ عَذَاباً
text: ‘So now taste! — in other words it will be said to them in the Hereafter when the chastisement has befallen them taste now your requital! For We will increase you in nothing but chastisement’ in addition to your due chastisement.

arabic: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازاً
text: Truly for the God-fearing there will be a triumph a place of triumph in Paradise

arabic: حَدَآئِقَ وَأَعْنَاباً
text: gardens orchards hadā’iqa is either a substitution for or an explication of mafāzan ‘a triumph’ and vineyards wa-a‘nāban is a supplement to mafāzan ‘a triumph’

arabic: وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَاباً
text: and buxom maidens kawā‘ib is the plural of kā‘ib of equal age atrāb is the plural of tirb

arabic: وَكَأْساً دِهَاقاً
text: and a brimming cup wine filling the vessels in which it is in; in sūrat al-Qitāl it is said and rivers of wine Q. 4715.

arabic: لاَّ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً وَلاَ كِذَّاباً
text: They will not hear in it that is in Paradise when they drink wine and in other situations any vain talk any words of falsehood or lies between one another read kidhāban to mean kadhiban ‘lies’ or kidhdhāban to mean takdhīban ‘lying’ in contrast to what happens in this world when wine is drunk

arabic: جَزَآءً مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَآءً حِسَاباً
text: this will be a reward from your Lord in other words God has rewarded them with this reward as a gift ‘atā’an substitutes for jazā’an ‘reward’ that is sufficing that is abundant hisāban as meaning ‘abundant’ derives from their saying a‘tānī fa-ahsabanī ‘he gave me so abundantly that I said “that is enough for me”’ hasbī

arabic: رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَاباً
text: from the Lord of the heavens and the earth read rabbi ‘from the Lord of’ or rabbu ‘He is the Lord of’ and all that is between them the Compassionate One likewise read rahmāni or rahmānu or read rahmānu with rabbi for the preceding Whom exalted be He they that is creatures will not be able to address that is to say not one of them will be able to address Him for fear of Him

arabic: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ صَفّاً لاَّ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَاباً
text: on the day yawma is the adverbial qualifier for lā yamlikūna ‘they will not be able to’ when the Spirit Gabriel or God’s hosts and the angels stand arrayed saffan is a circumstantial qualifier in other words mustaffīna. They creatures will not speak except him whom the Compassionate One permits to speak and who says what is right from among the believers and the angels as if meaning that they will intercede for he whom He approves of.

arabic: ذَلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ مَآباً
text: That is the True Day whose coming to pass is definite namely the Day of Resurrection. So whoever wishes to let him seek resort with his Lord a return to Him that is to say let him return to God by being obedient to Him so that he may be secure from chastisement in it.

arabic: إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَاباً قَرِيباً يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يٰلَيْتَنِي كُنتُ تُرَاباً
text: Lo! We have warned you O disbelievers of Mecca of a chastisement that is near the chastisement of the impending Day of Resurrection — for anything that is impending is also near — the day yawma adverbially qualifies ‘adhāban ‘a chastisement’ by describing it when a person when every person will behold what his hands have sent ahead of good and evil and the disbeliever will say ‘O yā is a particle used to call attention to something would that I were dust!’ in other words and not be chastised. He says this when God exalted be He says to the beasts after each of them has retaliated against the other ‘Be dust!’.

arabic: وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً
text: By those that wrest by the angels who wrest the souls of disbelievers violently;

arabic: وَٱلنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطاً
text: by those that draw out by the angels who draw out the souls of believers gently;

arabic: وَٱلسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحاً
text: by those that glide serenely by the angels who descend from the heavens with His command exalted be He;

arabic: فَٱلسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقاً
text: by those that race forward by the angels who race forward to Paradise with the souls of believers;

arabic: فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً
text: and by those that direct the affair by the angels who direct the affairs of this world that is to say they descend with the directions for it from God the response to all of these oath clauses has been omitted understood to be something like la-tub‘athunna yā kuffāra Makka ‘you shall certainly be resurrected O disbelievers of Mecca!’ which is also the operator of the following clause

arabic: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ
text: the day when the Tremor quakes that is to say the first blast as a result of which everything will be shaken violently thus it the subject has been described in terms of the effect it produces

arabic: تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ
text: and is followed by the Aftershock the second blast; between the two blasts is a span of forty years the sentence tatba‘uhā’l-rādifatu is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-rājifa ‘the Tremor’ in other words the ‘day’ can adverbially accommodate both blasts and other events and so for this reason it can also properly function as the adverbial qualifier for the Resurrection that will take place after the second blast;

arabic: قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ
text: on that day hearts will be trembling frightened and anxious

arabic: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ
text: their eyes humbled abject because of the terror that they see.

arabic: يَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي ٱلْحَافِرَةِ
text: They those of the mentioned hearts and eyes will say mockingly and in rejection of the Resurrection ‘Are we indeed read a-innā pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second and inserting an alif between them in both cases and in both instances being restored as before? Shall we be restored to life after death al-hāfira is a noun signifying the ‘first part’ of anything from which is derived the expression raja‘a fī hāfiratihi to mean that so and so ‘returned whence he had come’.

arabic: أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَّخِرَةً
text: What! When we have been decayed bones?’ nakhira a variant reading has nākhira ‘decayed and withered’ will we have life again?

arabic: قَالُواْ تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ
text: They will say ‘That return of ours to life then if it were true would be a ruinous return!’.

arabic: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
text: God exalted be He says But it the Aftershock which will be followed by the Resurrection will be only a single blast and so when it is blasted

arabic: فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ
text: behold then they all creatures will be upon the surface of the earth alive after having been dead inside it.

arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰ
text: Have you O Muhammad (s) received the story of Moses hadīthu Mūsā operates the clause that follows

arabic: إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
text: when his Lord called out to him in the holy valley of Tuwā? — this is the name of the valley it may be read with nunation Tuwan or without — and He said

arabic: ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ
text: ‘Go to Pharaoh; he has indeed become rebellious he has exceeded all bounds with his disbelief

arabic: فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
text: and say “Would you — I call you to — purify yourself tazakkā a variant reading has tazzakkā where the original second tā’ of tatazakkā has been assimilated with the zāy to purge yourself of idolatry by bearing witness that there is no god but God

arabic: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ
text: and allow me to guide you to your Lord to show you how to know Him ma‘rifa by way of proofs so that you may have fear of Him?” ’

arabic: فَأَرَاهُ ٱلآيَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
text: So he showed him the greatest sign from among His nine signs namely the glowing hand or the slithering staff.

arabic: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ
text: But he Pharaoh denied Moses and disobeyed God exalted be He.

arabic: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ
text: Then he turned his back to faith going about in haste throughout the land causing corruption.

arabic: فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَىٰ
text: Then he gathered he assembled the sorcerers and his armies and proclaimed

arabic: فَقَالَ أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
text: and said ‘I am your most high lord!’ above whom is no other lord.

arabic: فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ
text: So God seized him He destroyed him by drowning him as punishment for the latter that is to say these last words of his and for the former that is to say his saying previously ‘I do not know of any god for you other than me’ Q. 2838 — and between the two claims made by Pharaoh was an interval of forty years.

arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
text: Assuredly in that which is mentioned there is a moral for him who fears God exalted be He.

arabic: ءَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بَنَاهَا
text: Are you read a-antum pronouncing both hamzas or by substituting an alif for the second one not pronouncing it and inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the former or without this insertion namely you the deniers of the Resurrection harder to create or the heaven which He has built? harder to create banāhā an explication of the manner of its creation.

arabic: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا
text: He made it rise high — an explication of the manner of its construction; in other words He made its vertical extension high; it is also said that samkahā means ‘its ceiling’ — and levelled it He made it even flawless

arabic: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا
text: and darkened its night and brought forth its day He exposed the light of its sun ‘night’ has been annexed to it the heaven because it represents its shade and likewise the ‘sun’ because it represents its light;

arabic: وَٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا
text: and after that He spread out the earth He made it flat for it had been created before the heaven but without having been spread out;

arabic: أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَآءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا
text: from it He has brought forth akhraja a circumstantial qualifier with a suppressed preceding qad that is to say mukhrijan ‘bringing forth from it’ its waters by making its springs gush forth and its pastures what cattle graze of trees and herbage and what humans consume of foods and fruits the use of mar‘ā to express this of the earth is figurative

arabic: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا
text: and has set firm the mountains on the face of the earth so that it stays still

arabic: مَتَاعاً لَّكُمْ وَلأَنْعَامِكُمْ
text: as a source of sustenance an object denoting reason for an implied verbal clause in other words fa‘ala dhālika mut‘atan or tamtī‘an ‘He did this to provide a source of sustenance’ for you and your flocks an‘ām is the plural of na‘am which are camels cows and sheep.

arabic: فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
text: So when the Greatest Catastrophe befalls — the second blast —

arabic: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا سَعَىٰ
text: the day when man will remember yawma yatadhakkaru’l-insānu substitutes for idhā ‘when’ his efforts in the life of the world in the way of good or evil

arabic: وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ
text: and the Hell-fire the consuming Fire is revealed for all to see for every on-looker the response to idhā ‘when’ is what follows

arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ
text: as for him who was rebellious who disbelieved

arabic: وَآثَرَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
text: and preferred the life of this world by pursuing carnal desires

arabic: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
text: Hell-fire will indeed be the abode his abode.

arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
text: But as for him who feared the stance before his Lord his standing before Him and forbade the evil-bidding soul from pursuing desire that leads to perdition as a result of that person’s lusting after carnal desires

arabic: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ
text: Paradise will indeed be the abode in sum the response to idhā ‘when’ verse 34 is that the disobedient one will be in the Fire and the obedient one in Paradise.

arabic: يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَٰهَا
text: They that is the disbelievers of Mecca will ask you about the Hour when will it set in? when will it come to pass and when will it begin?

arabic: فِيمَ أَنتَ مِن ذِكْرَٰهَا
text: What have you to do with the mention of it? in other words you have no knowledge of it in order to mention it.

arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ مُنتَهَٰهَآ
text: With your Lord it belongs ultimately ultimate knowledge of it lies with Him; none other than Him has any knowledge of it.

arabic: إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَٰهَا
text: You are only a warner for your warning will only benefit the one who fears it.

arabic: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَٰهَا
text: The day they see it it will be as if they had only tarried in their graves for an evening or the morning thereof that is to say as if only one evening of a day or its morning the annexation of duhā ‘morning’ to ‘ashiyya ‘evening’ is valid on the basis of their contiguity since both constitute either side of the day; the annexation has also allowed for the word to fall in harmony with the end-rhyme of the verses.

arabic: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
text: He the Prophet frowned glowered with his face and turned away

arabic: أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ
text: because the blind man came to him ‘Abd Allāh son of Umm Maktūm who interrupted him while he was busy with those notables of Quryash whose submission to God he was very eager for. The blind man was not aware that he was busy with these and so he called out to him ‘Teach me of what God has taught you’. However the Prophet s went off to his house. He was then reproached for this with what was revealed in this sūra. Afterwards whenever he came to him the Prophet would say to him ‘Greetings to him on whose account God reproached me!’ and would lay down his cloak for him.

arabic: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ
text: And how would you know? Perhaps he would cleanse himself yazzakkā the original tā’ of yatazakkā has been assimilated with the zāy that is perhaps he would purge himself of sins by what he hears from you

arabic: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
text: or be admonished yadhdhakkar the original tā’ of yatadhakkar has been assimilated with the dhāl and so the reminder the admonition heard from you might benefit him a variant reading for tanfa‘uhu has tanfa‘ahu as the response to the optative statement.

arabic: أَمَّا مَنِ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
text: But as for the one who thinks himself self-sufficient through wealth

arabic: فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ
text: to him you do attend tasaddā a variant reading has tassaddā where the original second tā’ of tatasaddā has been assimilated with the sād him you accept and turn your attention to;

arabic: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلاَّ يَزَّكَّىٰ
text: yet it is not your concern if he does not cleanse himself if he does not believe.

arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن جَآءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ
text: But as for him who comes to you hurrying yas‘ā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb jā’a ‘comes’

arabic: وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ
text: fearful of God wa-huwa yakhshā is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb yas‘ā ‘hurrying’ — this being the blind man —

arabic: فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ
text: to him you pay no heed talahhā the original second tā’ of tatalahhā has been omitted that is to say from him you are distracted by other things.

arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ
text: No indeed! do not behave like this. Truly it the sūra is or the verses are a reminder an admonition for all creatures —

arabic: فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ
text: so let whoever will remember it preserve it in his memory and thus be admonished by it —

arabic: فَي صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ
text: on leaves fī suhufin is the second predicate of innahā ‘truly it’ and what precedes it is a parenthetical statement that are honoured by God

arabic: مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ
text: elevated in the heavens purified exalted above the touch of devils

arabic: بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ
text: in the hands of scribes who write it down from the Preserved Tablet

arabic: كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ
text: noble pious obedient to God exalted be He these being the angels.

arabic: قُتِلَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ
text: Perish man! accursed be the disbeliever! What has made him ungrateful? an interrogative statement meant as a rebuke — what has driven him to disbelief?

arabic: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيءٍ خَلَقَهُ
text: From what thing has He created him? an interrogative meant as an affirmative which He then explains by saying

arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ
text: From a drop of sperm did He create him then proportion him in stages as a blood-clot then an embryo up to the last stage of his creation.

arabic: ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ
text: Then He made the way his exit from his mother’s belly easy for him;

arabic: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ
text: then He makes him die and buries him He places him in a grave that hides him;

arabic: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُ
text: then when He wills He will raise him for the Resurrection.

arabic: كَلاَّ لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَآ أَمَرَهُ
text: No indeed! Verily he has not accomplished he has not done what He his Lord commanded him to do.

arabic: فَلْيَنظُرِ ٱلإِنسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ
text: So let man consider in reflection his source of food how it is determined and procured for him

arabic: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبّاً
text: that We pour down water from the clouds plenteously;

arabic: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلأَرْضَ شَقّاً
text: then We split the earth into fissures with vegetation

arabic: فَأَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبّاً
text: and cause the grains such as wheat and barley to grow therein

arabic: وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً
text: and vines and herbs qadb is moist qatt

arabic: وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلاً
text: and olives and date-palms

arabic: وَحَدَآئِقَ غُلْباً
text: and gardens of dense foliage orchards teeming with trees

arabic: وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبّاً
text: and fruits and pastures abb is what cattle graze; it is also said to be ‘straw’

arabic: مَّتَاعاً لَّكُمْ وَلأَنْعَامِكُمْ
text: as sustenance understand matā‘an as mut‘atan or tamtī‘an as explained above in the previous sūra for you and your flocks also as explained above.

arabic: فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلصَّآخَّةُ
text: So when the deafening Cry the second blast comes —

arabic: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ
text: the day when a man will flee from his own brother

arabic: وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ
text: and his mother and his father

arabic: وَصَٰحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ
text: and his wife and his sons yawma ‘the day when’ is a substitution for idhā ‘when’ the response to which is indicated by what follows —

arabic: لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ
text: every person that day will have a matter to preoccupy him a predicament to distract him from the affairs of others in other words every person will be preoccupied with his own self.

arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ
text: On that day some faces will be shining radiant

arabic: ضَاحِكَةٌ مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌ
text: laughing joyous happy — these are the believers.

arabic: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ
text: And some faces on that day will be covered with dust

arabic: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ
text: overcast covered with gloom darkness and blackness.

arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَفَرَةُ ٱلْفَجَرَةُ
text: Those the people of this predicament are the disbelievers the profligates those who have combined disbelief with profligacy.

arabic: إِذَا ٱلشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ
text: When the sun is folded away enfolded and stripped of its light

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ ٱنكَدَرَتْ
text: and when the stars scatter when they are extinguished and hurtle down towards the earth

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ
text: and when the mountains are set in motion when they are blown away from the face of the earth becoming as scattered dust

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ
text: and when the pregnant camels are neglected abandoned without a herdsman or anyone to milk them on account of the matter that has come over them — even though previously no wealth was dearer to them than these pregnant camels;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ
text: and when the wild beasts are mustered when they are brought together after being resurrected so that each of them may retaliate against the other before becoming dust;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ
text: and when the seas are set afire read sujirat or sujjirat when they are set alight and become a mass of fire;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ
text: and when the souls are coupled when they are paired up with their bodies;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ
text: and when the girl buried-alive the young girl buried alive for fear of shame and impoverishment asks — in rebuke of its slayer —

arabic: بِأَىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ
text: for what sin she was slain sa’alat ‘asks’ a variant reading has su’ilat ‘she is asked’ narrating the address directed to her to which she then responds by saying ‘I was slain without having committed any sin’;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ
text: and when the scrolls the scrolls containing the deeds are unrolled read nushirat or nushshirat when they are unfolded and spread out;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ
text: and when the heaven is stripped off torn away from its place just as the skin of a sheep is stripped off;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ
text: and when the Hell-fire is set ablaze read su‘irat or su‘‘irat when it is set alight;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ
text: and when Paradise is brought near when it is brought close to those who have merited it that they may enter it the response to idhā ‘when’ at the beginning of the sūra and all that has been supplemented thereto is the following

arabic: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّآ أَحْضَرَتْ
text: then a soul every soul at the time of the occurrence of the things mentioned which is the Day of Resurrection will know what it has presented of good or evil.

arabic: فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلْخُنَّسِ
text: So I swear fa-lā lā is extra by the receding planets

arabic: ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْكُنَّسِ
text: the movers the setters that is the five planets Saturn Jupiter Mars Venus and Mercury takhnusu means ‘they sink away’ during their orbit whereas we see stars at the end of their zodiacal course return to the start; taknisu means that they enter their kinās ‘hideaway’ in other words they retreat into their setting-places;

arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ
text: and by the night as it approaches as it falls with its darkness or it means as it recedes;

arabic: وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ
text: and by the dawn as it breathes as it extends until it becomes broad daylight

arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ
text: truly this Qur’ān is the word of a messenger who is noble in the sight of God exalted be He — this being the messenger Gabriel it qawl ‘word’ has been annexed to him because he descends with it

arabic: ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِندَ ذِي ٱلْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ
text: powerful one of mighty powers eminent one of eminent status makīnin is semantically connected ‘inda ‘in the presence of’ in the presence of the Lord of the Throne that is God exalted be He;

arabic: مُّطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ
text: obeyed there the angels obey him in the heavens trustworthy with the Revelation.

arabic: وَمَا صَاحِبُكُمْ بِمَجْنُونٍ
text: And your companion Muhammad (s) wa-mā sāhibukum a supplement to the clause from innahu ‘truly this is’ up to the last of the oath clauses is not a madman as you claim.

arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِٱلأُفُقِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
text: For verily he Muhammad (s) saw him Gabriel in the form in which he was created on the clear horizon the highest one towards the east;

arabic: وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ
text: and he Muhammad (s) is not to be accused of knowing the Unseen what is hidden of the revelation and the tidings of the heaven a variant reading for bi-zanīnin has bi-danīnin meaning that he is not ‘niggardly’ with the Unseen so as to reduce something of it and not disclose it.

arabic: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍ
text: And it that is the Qur’ān is not the word of an accursed satan eavesdropping stealthily.

arabic: فَأيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ
text: So where are you going? So what path are you going to follow in repudiating the Qur’ān and turning away from it?

arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
text: It is only a reminder an admonition for all worlds those of mankind and jinn

arabic: لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَسْتَقِيمَ
text: for those of you who li-man shā’a minkum is a substitution for li’l-‘ālamīna ‘for all worlds’ using the same preposition wish to go straight by following the truth;

arabic: وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
text: but you will not wish to go straight along the path of truth unless God the Lord of the Worlds of all creatures wills that you should go straight along it.

arabic: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ
text: When the heaven is split open when it is rent asunder

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْكَوَاكِبُ ٱنتَثَرَتْ
text: and when the stars are dispersed when they expire and begin to fall

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ
text: and when the seas are burst forth released one upon the other forming one mass of water so that the sweet water mixes with the salty;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ
text: and when the tombs are overturned when their earth above them is dug up and its dead are raised the response to idhā ‘when’ and all that is supplemented thereto is the following

arabic: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ
text: a soul every soul will know at the time of the occurrence of the things mentioned which is the Day of Resurrection what it has sent ahead in the way of deeds and what it has left behind of these and did not do.

arabic: يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلإِنسَٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ
text: O disbelieving man! What has deceived you with regard to your generous Lord? so that you have disobeyed Him

arabic: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ
text: Who created you when you were not then made you upright in your created form with sound limbs then proportioned you read fa-‘adalak or fa-‘addalak making you symmetrical in shape with well-proportioned parts so that no hand or leg is longer than the other

arabic: فِيۤ أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
text: assembling you in whatever mā is a relative form He will?

arabic: كَلاَّ بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ
text: No indeed! — a deterrent against letting oneself be misled by the generosity of God exalted be He. Rather you that is disbelievers of Mecca deny Judgement requital for deeds;

arabic: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ
text: Yet lo! there are above you watchers from among the angels over your deeds

arabic: كِرَاماً كَاتِبِينَ
text: noble in God’s sight writers of these deeds

arabic: يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ
text: who know whatever you do all of it.

arabic: إِنَّ ٱلأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ
text: Indeed the pious the believers who are sincere in their faith shall be amid bliss in Paradise

arabic: وَإِنَّ ٱلْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ
text: and indeed the profligates the disbelievers shall be in Hell-fire a scorching fire

arabic: يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ
text: entering it to suffer its heat on the Day of Judgement the Day of Requital

arabic: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَآئِبِينَ
text: and they shall not be absent from it they shall not be taken out of it.

arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
text: And what would show you what would inform you what the Day of Judgement is?

arabic: ثُمَّ مَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
text: Again what would show you what the Day of Judgement is? — repeated to emphasise its enormity.

arabic: يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً وَٱلأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ
text: It is a day read yawmu when no soul will be of any avail any use to another soul and the absolute command on that day will be God’s there will be no power of command for anyone other than Him thereat in other words none has been given the power to mediate thereupon in contrast to situations in this world.

arabic: وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ
text: Woe waylun a term entailing chastisement; or it is the name of a valley in Hell to the defrauders

arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ٱكْتَالُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ
text: those who when they take measure from people demand it in full the measure;

arabic: وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ
text: but who when they measure for them or weigh for them they cause them loss they diminish for them the measure or the weight.

arabic: أَلا يَظُنُّ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَّبْعُوثُونَ
text: Do such individuals not know for certain alā indicates an interrogative of rebuke that they will be resurrected

arabic: لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
text: for an awful day that is to say on it and this is the Day of Resurrection

arabic: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
text: a day when yawma is a substitution for the syntactical locus of li-yawmin ‘to an awful day’ and as such is in the accusative because of the verb mab‘ūthūna ‘will be resurrected’ mankind will rise from their graves before the Lord of the Worlds? the Lord of all creatures for His affair His reckoning and His requital.

arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّ كِتَابَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ
text: Nay! verily the record of the profligates that is to say the record of the deeds of the disbelievers is in Sijjīn — this is said to be a book containing the record of all the deeds of the devils and the disbelievers; but it is also said to be a location in the lowermost part of the seventh earth the place of Satan and his hosts.

arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِجِّينٌ
text: And what would tell you what Sijjīn is? what the book of Sijjīn is.

arabic: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ
text: It is a sealed book.

arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
text: Woe to the deniers on that day

arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
text: who deny the Day of Judgement the Day of Requital alladhīna yukadhdhibūna bi-yawmi’l-dīn either a substitution for or an explication of al-mukadhdhibīna ‘the deniers’;

arabic: وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلاَّ كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
text: and none deny it but every sinful the form athīm is hyperbolic transgressor overstepping the bounds.

arabic: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ
text: When Our signs of the Qur’ān are recited to him he says ‘Mere fables asātīr of the ancients!’ mere tales that were written down sutirat in ancient times asātīr is the plural of ustūra or istāra.

arabic: كَلاَّ بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ
text: No indeed! — a deterrent and a warning against saying such things. Rather there has slayed engulfed their hearts covering them like rust that which they earned of acts of disobedience.

arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ عَن رَّبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّمَحْجُوبُونَ
text: Nay! verily they on that day the Day of Resurrection will be screened off from their Lord and so they will not see Him.

arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُواْ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text: Then they will be exposed to Hell-fire then they will enter the scorching Fire;

arabic: ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ
text: then it will be said to them ‘This that is the chastisement is that which you used to deny!’

arabic: كَلاَّ إِنَّ كِتَابَ ٱلأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ
text: Nay! verily the record of the pious that is the record of the deeds of the believers who were sincere in their faith is in ‘Illiyyūn — this is said to be the book containing all the good deeds of the angels and the believers from among the two heavy ones sc. mankind and jinn; but it is also said to be a place below the Throne in the seventh heaven;

arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ
text: and what will tell you what will inform you what ‘Illiyyūn is? what the book of ‘Illiyyūn is.

arabic: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ
text: It is a sealed book

arabic: يَشْهَدُهُ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ
text: witnessed by those brought near from among the angels.

arabic: إِنَّ ٱلأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ
text: Assuredly the pious will be amid bliss in Paradise

arabic: عَلَى ٱلأَرَآئِكِ يَنظُرُونَ
text: upon couches upon beds beneath canopies gazing at the bliss which they have been given.

arabic: تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
text: You will perceive in their faces the radiancy of bliss the splendour and beauty of blissfulness

arabic: يُسْقَوْنَ مِن رَّحِيقٍ مَّخْتُومٍ
text: as they are given to drink a nectar a wine free of any impurities that is sealed in its vessel none other than them breaking its seal

arabic: خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ وَفِي ذَلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ ٱلْمُتَنَافِسُونَ
text: whose seal is musk that is whose final sip is followed by an emanating scent of musk — so for such bliss let the viers vie let them desire to apply themselves to obedience of God —

arabic: وَمِزَاجُهُ مِن تَسْنِيمٍ
text: and whose mixture that is to say that with which it is mixed is of Tasnīm which is explained by His following words

arabic: عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ
text: a spring ‘aynan is in the accusative because of an implicit prefatory amdahu ‘I extol this spring’ from which those brought near will drink yashrabu bihā should be yashrabu minhā or it may be that bihā is used because yashrabu is meant to imply the sense of yaltadhdhu bihā ‘in which they delight’.

arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُواْ كَانُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَضْحَكُونَ
text: Verily the guilty like Abū Jahl and his ilk used to laugh at the believers such as ‘Ammār b. Yāsir and Bilāl the Ethiopian and those like them in mockery of them;

arabic: وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ
text: and when they the believers passed them by they would wink at one another the guilty beckoned with their eyebrows and eyelids towards the believers in mockery;

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمُ ٱنقَلَبُواْ فَكِهِينَ
text: and when they returned to their folks they would return blithely fākihīna a variant reading has fakihīna rejoicing in their disparaging mention of the believers;

arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ لَضَالُّونَ
text: and when they see them that is the believers they say ‘Lo! these men are astray!’ on account of their belief in Muhammad (s).

arabic: وَمَآ أُرْسِلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ
text: God exalted be He says Yet they that is the disbelievers were not sent as watchers over them over the believers to preserve them or to keep a record of their deeds and thus guide them back to what is best for them.

arabic: فَٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ
text: So today that is the Day of Resurrection the believers will be laughing at the disbelievers

arabic: عَلَى ٱلأَرَآئِكِ يَنظُرُونَ
text: upon couches in Paradise gazing out from their dwellings at the disbelievers while they are being tortured; and they will laugh at them just as they the disbelievers had laughed at them in the world.

arabic: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ ٱلْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ
text: Have the disbelievers been requited for what they used to do? Yes indeed!

arabic: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ
text: When the heaven is rent asunder

arabic: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ
text: and heeds gives ear to and in rending itself asunder obeys its Lord as it should that is as its duty is to heed and obey

arabic: وَإِذَا ٱلأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ
text: and when the earth is stretched out when its width is increased just as a piece of leather is stretched so that no edifice or mountain remains upon it

arabic: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ
text: and casts out all that is in it of the dead onto its surface and empties itself thereof

arabic: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ
text: and heeds and in this respect gives ear to and obeys its Lord as it should all of this will be on the Day of Resurrection the response to idhā ‘when’ and to all that is supplemented thereto has been omitted; but it is indicated by what follows it and is implied to be something like laqiya’l-insānu ‘amalahu ‘man will encounter his deeds’.

arabic: يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحاً فَمُلاَقِيهِ
text: O man! Verily you are labouring exerting your efforts toward the encounter with your Lord that is death laboriously and you will encounter it that is you will encounter your mentioned good or evil deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَـٰبَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ
text: Then as for him who is given his book the record of his deeds in his right hand — and this is the believer —

arabic: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَاباً يَسِيراً
text: he will receive an easy reckoning which simply entails the presentation of his deeds to him as in the hadīth of the two Sahīhs of Bukhārī and Muslim — in which there is also a hadīth saying ‘He who is reckoned with at length will be destined for perdition’ — and after this presentation of his deeds to the believer he will be excused

arabic: وَيَنقَلِبُ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً
text: and return to his family in Paradise joyful because of it.

arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِ
text: But as for him who is given his book from behind his back — and this is the disbeliever whose right hand is chained to his neck and whose left hand by which he is given the book is placed behind his back

arabic: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُواْ ثُبُوراً
text: he will pray upon seeing what is in it for annihilation he will invoke destruction against himself by saying yā thabūrāh ‘O annihilation of mine!’

arabic: وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيراً
text: and he will enter the Blaze an intense fire a variant reading for yaslā ‘he will enter’ has yusallā ‘he will be admitted’.

arabic: إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِيۤ أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً
text: Indeed among his folk his clan in the world he used to be joyful wanton lusting after his desires;

arabic: إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ
text: indeed he thought that an softened in place of the hardened form with its subject omitted that is to say annahu he would never return to his Lord.

arabic: بَلَىٰ إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيراً
text: Nay! he will return to Him; indeed his Lord is ever Seer of him knowing that he would return to Him.

arabic: فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلشَّفَقِ
text: So I swear fa-lā lā is extra by the twilight al-shafaq the reddishness visible in the horizon after the sunset

arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ
text: and by the night and what it envelops what it brings together of creatures and otherwise that have entered into it

arabic: وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا ٱتَّسَقَ
text: and by the moon when it is at the full and its light is complete and this happens during the nights of the full moon

arabic: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقاً عَن طَبقٍ
text: you will surely journey tarkabunna is actually tarkabūnanna but the nūn of the indicative has been omitted because of two identical letters following one another and the wāw is omitted because of two unvocalised consonants coming together from stage to stage state after state namely death then life then what comes afterwards of the states at the Resurrection.

arabic: فَمَا لَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ
text: So what is wrong with them that is the disbelievers that they do not have faith that is to say what is there to prevent them from embracing faith; or what argument do they have for neglecting it despite the existence of proofs for it

arabic: وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْآنُ لاَ يَسْجُدُونَ
text: and what is wrong with them that when the Qur’ān is recited to them they do not prostrate? they do not submit by believing in it given its inimitability?

arabic: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُكَذِّبُونَ
text: Nay but the disbelievers deny resurrection and other matters

arabic: وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ
text: and God knows best what they are amassing accumulating in their scrolls in the way of disbelief denial and evil deeds.

arabic: فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
text: So give them good tidings inform them of a painful chastisement

arabic: إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
text: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds theirs will be an unfailing reward one that is unending undiminished and not given to them in expectance of anything in return.

arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْبُرُوجِ
text: By the heaven of the constellations the twelve constellations of the planets — as explained in sūrat al-Furqān Q. 2561;

arabic: وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْمَوْعُودِ
text: and by the promised day the Day of Resurrection;

arabic: وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ
text: and by the witness Friday and the witnessed the day of ‘Arafa — that is how these three elements have been explained in hadīth for the first one is ‘promised’ the second one is ‘a witness’ that testifies to deeds performed in it while the third is ‘witnessed’ by mankind and angels the introductory particle of the response to the oath has been omitted but is implied to be laqad ‘verily’ sc. laqad qutila ashābu’l-ukhdūd

arabic: قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأُخْدُودِ
text: perish accursed be the men of the ditch! the pit in the ground

arabic: ٱلنَّارِ ذَاتِ ٱلْوَقُودِ
text: of the fire al-nāri is an inclusive substitution of it al-ukhdūdi ‘of the ditch’ abounding in fuel by which it was fuelled

arabic: إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ
text: when they sat by it around the edge of the ditch on chairs

arabic: وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ
text: and they themselves to what they did to those who believed in God in the way of torturing them by hurling them into the fire when they did not recant their faith were witnesses they were themselves present thereat. It is reported in a hadīth that God saved the believers who had been thrown into the fire by taking their souls before they fell into it and that the fire then rose up and burnt all those sitting around it.

arabic: وَمَا نَقَمُواْ مِنْهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ
text: And all that they were vindicative towards them of was that they believed in God the Mighty in His kingdom the Praised

arabic: ٱلَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
text: to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and God is Witness to all things in other words all that the disbelievers disavowed of the believers was their faith.

arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَتَنُواْ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُواْ فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
text: Indeed those who persecute believing men and believing women by having them burnt then do not repent there will be for them the chastisement of Hell in return for their disbelief and there will also be for them the chastisement of burning that is to say the chastisement for their having had the believers burnt in the Hereafter; but it is also said that there is this chastisement for them in this world as when the fire rose up and burnt them as mentioned above.

arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ ذَلِكَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْكَبِيرُ
text: Indeed those who believe and perform righteous deeds for them there will be gardens underneath which rivers flow that is the supreme triumph.

arabic: إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ
text: Assuredly your Lord’s assault against the disbelievers is severe as severe as He will it to be.

arabic: إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِىءُ وَيُعِيدُ
text: Assuredly it is He Who originates creation and restores and is never thwarted in what He wills

arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلْوَدُودُ
text: and He is the Forgiving to sinning believers the Loving the One Who shows love to His friends through His acts of generosity

arabic: ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْمَجِيدُ
text: Lord of the Throne its Creator and Possessor the Glorious read nominative al-majīdu the One deserving of the perfect attributes of sublimity

arabic: فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ
text: Doer of what He desires nothing able to thwart Him.

arabic: هَلُ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ٱلْجُنُودِ
text: Have you O Muhammad (s) received the story of the hosts

arabic: فِرْعَوْنَ وَثَمُودَ
text: Pharaoh and Thamūd? Fir‘awna wa-Thamūda substitutes for al-junūdi — the mention of ‘Pharaoh’ suffices to also include his followers; their ‘story’ is that they were destroyed for their disbelief and this is meant as a warning for those who deny the Prophet s and the Qur’ān that they may be admonished thereby.

arabic: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي تَكْذِيبٍ
text: Nay but the disbelievers are engrossed in denial of the mentioned;

arabic: وَٱللَّهُ مِن وَرَآئِهِمْ مُّحِيطٌ
text: and God is behind them All-Encompassing — they have no protector against Him.

arabic: بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌ مَّجِيدٌ
text: Nay but it is a glorious a magnificent Qur’ān

arabic: فِي لَوْحٍ مَّحْفُوظٍ
text: in a tablet suspended above the seventh heaven preserved read mahfūzin from all devils and from having any of its contents altered; it is a high as the distance between the earth and the heaven and as wide as the distance between the east and the west made of white pearls — as stated by Ibn ‘Abbās may God be pleased with both him and his father ‘Abbās

arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلطَّارِقِ
text: By the heaven and the night-visitor! al-tāriq actually denotes any thing that comes by night including stars because they come out at night.

arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلطَّارِقُ
text: And what will tell you what the night-visitor is? mā’l-tāriq is a subject and predicate standing as the second object of the verb adrā ‘tell’; and what comes after the first mā ‘what’ is the predicate thereof of this first mā — this statement emphasises the magnificence of the ‘night-visitor’ which is explained in what follows. It is

arabic: ٱلنَّجْمُ ٱلثَّاقِبُ
text: The piercing the brilliant because of its piercing the darkness with its light star! meaning the constellation Pleiades; or it refers to all stars the response to the oath follows

arabic: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ
text: Over every soul there is a keeper if read la-mā then mā is extra and in is softened in place of the hardened form with its subject omitted that is to say innahu; the lām is a particle for separation; if read lammā then in is for negation and lammā means illā ‘except that’ — the watcher is an angel that keeps a record of its deeds both the good and the evil.

arabic: فَلْيَنظُرِ ٱلإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ
text: So let man consider by way of reflection from what he was created from what thing

arabic: خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ
text: the response is He was created from a gushing fluid gushing forth from the man and the woman into the womb

arabic: يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ
text: issuing from between the loins of the man and the breast-bones of the woman.

arabic: إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ
text: Assuredly He exalted be He is able to bring him back to resurrect man after his death; and so when he reflects on his origins he will realise that the One who was able to do this is also able to resurrect him

arabic: يَوْمَ تُبْلَىٰ ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ
text: on the day when all secrets the hidden convictions and intentions of the hearts are inspected when they are examined and revealed

arabic: فَمَا لَهُ مِن قُوَّةٍ وَلاَ نَاصِرٍ
text: whereat he the one who denies resurrection will have neither strength to defend himself against chastisement nor any helper to avert it from him.

arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلرَّجْعِ
text: By the heaven of returns of the rain that returns time and again

arabic: وَٱلأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ
text: and by the earth of fissures splitting with the growth of vegetation

arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ
text: assuredly it the Qur’ān is a decisive word distinguishing between truth and falsehood

arabic: وَمَا هوَ بِٱلْهَزْلِ
text: and it is not a jest frivolity or falsehood.

arabic: إِنَّهُمْ يَكِيدُونَ كَيْداً
text: Indeed they that is the disbelievers are devising a plot they are preparing plots against the Prophet s

arabic: وَأَكِيدُ كَيْداً
text: and I too am devising a plot drawing them by degrees towards destruction from whence they know not.

arabic: فَمَهِّلِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً
text: So respite O Muhammad (s) the disbelievers; grant them respite reiterated as an emphasis one enhanced by the use of a different form mahhil amhil that is to say put them off for a little ruwaydā is a verbal noun emphasising the import of the operator and is the diminutive form of rūd or irwad with shortening of final consonant ruwaydan ruwaydā. Surely enough God exalted be He seized them at Badr and abrogated the dispensation of ‘granting respite’ by the ‘sword’ verse in other words by the command to fight and struggle.

arabic: سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ
text: Glorify the Name of your Lord that is exalt your Lord above what does not befit Him ism in isma rabbika ‘the Name of your Lord’ is extra the Most High an adjective qualifying rabbika ‘your Lord’

arabic: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ
text: Who created and proportioned His creature making it of well-proportioned parts without irregularities

arabic: وَٱلَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ
text: and Who determined what He wants and guided to what He had determined of good or evil

arabic: وَٱلَّذِيۤ أَخْرَجَ ٱلْمَرْعَىٰ
text: and Who brought forth the pasture Who caused herbage to grow

arabic: فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أَحْوَىٰ
text: then made it after verdancy blackened stubble desiccated broken chaff.

arabic: سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلاَ تَنسَىٰ
text: We will have you recite the Qur’ān so that you will not forget what you recite

arabic: إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ
text: except what God may will that you forget by abrogating its recitation and its ruling — the Prophet s used to recite aloud while Gabriel recited fearing to forget and so it is as though it was said to him ‘Do not hasten in it; you will not forget and so do not weary yourself by reciting it aloud’; assuredly He exalted be He knows what is overt of words and deeds and what is hidden of both of these.

arabic: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
text: And We will ease your way to the easy way the uncomplicated Law namely Islam.

arabic: فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
text: So remind admonish by the Qur’ān in case the reminder should be of benefit to the one whom you might remind the one mentioned in the following verse ‘he who fears will be reminded’ in other words even if it might not be of benefit for it is of benefit to some but of no benefit to others.

arabic: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ
text: He who fears God exalted be He will be reminded by it as in the verse So admonish by the Qur’ān him who fears My threat Q. 5045;

arabic: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَشْقَى
text: but the wretched one al-ashqā means al-shaqī that is to say the disbeliever will shun it that is the reminder in other words he will leave it aside not looking at it

arabic: ٱلَّذِى يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ
text: he who will be roasted in the greater Fire the Fire of the Hereafter the lesser fire being that of this world;

arabic: ثُمَّ لاَ يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يَحْيَا
text: then he will neither die therein and find rest nor live a enjoyable life.

arabic: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
text: Successful winner indeed is he who purifies himself who cleanses himself by means of his adherence to faith

arabic: وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ
text: and mentions the Name of his Lord saying Allāhu akbar ‘God is Great’ and prays the five prayers — and such are the concerns of one working towards the Hereafter concerns which the Meccan disbelievers shun.

arabic: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
text: Nay but you prefer or read yu’thirūna ‘they prefer’ the life of this world to the Hereafter

arabic: وَٱلآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
text: whereas the Hereafter and the Paradise it entails is better and more lasting.

arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِي ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلأُولَىٰ
text: Truly this the success of those who purify themselves and the Hereafter being better is in the former scrolls the ones revealed before the Qur’ān

arabic: صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ
text: the scrolls of Abraham and Moses the ten scrolls of Abraham and the Torah of Moses.

arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ٱلْغَاشِيَةِ
text: Has there — there has indeed — come to you the tiding of the Enveloper? the Resurrection so called because it ‘envelops’ creatures with its terrors.

arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ
text: Some faces on that day — they faces are used to represent the individuals in both instances — will be humbled abject

arabic: عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ
text: toiling weary tired and exhausted from the chains and fetters

arabic: تَصْلَىٰ نَاراً حَامِيَةً
text: roasting read taslā or tuslā in a scorching fire

arabic: تُسْقَىٰ مِنْ عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ
text: made to drink from a boiling spring one of extremely hot temperatures.

arabic: لَّيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مِن ضَرِيعٍ
text: They will have no food except cactus darī‘ — a type of thorn plant which no animal grazes on because of its vileness —

arabic: لاَّ يُسْمِنُ وَلاَ يُغْنِي مِن جُوعٍ
text: neither nourishing nor availing against hunger.

arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاعِمَةٌ
text: Other faces on that day will be delicate fair

arabic: لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ
text: pleased by their efforts in the life of the world expended in obedience pleased in the Hereafter upon seeing the reward thereof;

arabic: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ
text: in a lofty Garden lofty in a physical as well as an abstract sense

arabic: لاَّ تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لاَغِيَةً
text: in which they will not hear read lā yusma‘u ‘will not be heard’ or lā tasma‘u ‘they will not hear’ any vanity any inane soul speaking drivel;

arabic: فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ
text: therein is a running spring of water meaning ‘springs’;

arabic: فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ
text: therein are lofty couches lofty in terms of their essence their size and physical location

arabic: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ
text: and goblets vessels without handles set around the edges of the springs prepared for them to drink with

arabic: وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ
text: and cushions arrayed one next to the other against which they may lean

arabic: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ
text: and carpets rugs of velvet-hair spread out.

arabic: أَفَلاَ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلإِبْلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ
text: Will they the Meccan disbelievers not consider by way of reflection the camels how they are created?

arabic: وَإِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ
text: And the heaven how it was raised?

arabic: وَإِلَىٰ ٱلْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ
text: And the mountains how they were set?

arabic: وَإِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ
text: And the earth how it was laid out flat? and thus infer from this the power of God exalted be He and His Oneness? The commencing with the mention of camels is because they are closer in contact with it the earth than any other animal. As for His words sutihat ‘laid out flat’ this on a literal reading suggests that the earth is flat which is the opinion of most of the scholars of the revealed Law and not a sphere as astronomers ahl al-hay’a have it even if this latter does not contradict any of the pillars of the Law.

arabic: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ
text: So remind them of God’s graces and the proofs affirming His Oneness. For you are only an admonisher;

arabic: لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ
text: you are not a taskmaster over them a variant reading for musaytir has musaytir that is to say not one who has been given authority over them — this was revealed before the command to struggle against the disbelievers.

arabic: إِلاَّ مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ
text: But he who turns away he who rejects faith and disbelieves in the Qur’ān

arabic: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلأَكْبَرَ
text: God will chastise him with the greater chastisement the chastisement of the Hereafter the lesser chastisement being that of this world that of being killed or taken captive.

arabic: إِنَّ إِلَيْنَآ إِيَابَهُمْ
text: Truly to Us will be their return their coming back after death

arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُمْ
text: then truly with Us will lie their reckoning their requital which We will never abandon.

arabic: وَٱلْفَجْرِ
text: By the dawn that is to say by the dawn of each day

arabic: وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ
text: and by the ten nights the first ten nights of Dhū’l-Hijja

arabic: وَٱلشَّفْعِ وَٱلْوَتْرِ
text: and by the even the pair and the odd read watr or witr two alternative forms the single

arabic: وَٱلَّيلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ
text: and by the night in motion falling or receding

arabic: هَلْ فِي ذَلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ
text: Is there in that oath an oath for one of sense? one of intellect the response to the oath has been omitted that is to say it is to be understood as something like la-tu‘adhdhabunna yā kuffāra Makka ‘you will assuredly be chastised O disbelievers of Mecca!’.

arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
text: Have you not seen do you not know O Muhammad (s) how your Lord dealt with ‘Ād

arabic: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ
text: Iram — these were the former people of ‘Ād Irama is an explicative supplement or a substitution and it is treated as a diptote because it is a proper noun and feminine — of the towering ones that is to say the tall ones — the tallest one among them would reach four hundred cubits —

arabic: ٱلَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ
text: the like of which was not created in the land in terms of their power of assault and strength

arabic: وَثَمُودَ ٱلَّذِينَ جَابُواْ ٱلصَّخْرَ بِٱلْوَادِ
text: and Thamūd who hollowed hewed the rocks sakhr is the plural of sakhra in the valley the Wādī al-Qurā rocks which they used as dwellings

arabic: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلأَوْتَادِ
text: and Pharaoh the one of the tent-pegs he used to fasten four pegs and tie to these the hands and feet of those whom he tortured —

arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ
text: those who were rebellious became tyrannical in the land

arabic: فَأَكْثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلْفَسَادَ
text: and caused much corruption therein? by way of slaying and otherwise.

arabic: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ
text: So your Lord poured on them a scourge of chastisement.

arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ
text: Assuredly your Lord is ever on the watch watching over the deeds of servants nothing of which escapes Him that He may then requite them for these deeds.

arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلإِنسَانُ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَكْرَمَنِ
text: And as for man the disbeliever whenever his Lord tests him and honours him with wealth and other things and is gracious to him he says ‘My Lord has honoured me’.

arabic: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبْتَلاَهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيۤ أَهَانَنِ
text: But when he tests him and restricts his provision for him he says ‘My Lord has humiliated me’.

arabic: كَلاَّ بَل لاَّ تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
text: No indeed! — a disavowal of this notion in other words honour is not about wealth nor is there any humiliation in poverty rather it has to do with obedience and disobedience respectively; but the disbelievers of Mecca unmindful of this. Rather they do not honour the orphan they do not treat him with kindness despite their wealth or it means that they do not give him what is his due from an inheritance

arabic: وَلاَ تَحَآضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
text: and they do not urge neither themselves nor others the feeding of the needy;

arabic: وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلاً لَّمّاً
text: and they devour inheritance turāth means mīrāth greedily lamman that is to say voraciously when they appropriate lammuhum the women’s and the young ones’ share of the inheritance together with their own share of it or to their own wealth;

arabic: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبّاً جَمّاً
text: and they love wealth with abounding love that is to say greatly and so they do not expend any of it a variant reading in the case of all four verbs has the second person plural.

arabic: كَلاَّ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ دَكّاً دَكّاً
text: No indeed! — a deterrent for them from such conduct. When the earth is pulverised repeatedly when it is shaken until every edifice has collapsed and is destroyed

arabic: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلْمَلَكُ صَفّاً صَفّاً
text: and your Lord that is to say His command and the angels arrive rank on rank saffan saffan is a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘standing in rows’ or ‘made up of many ranks’

arabic: وَجِيۤءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلإِنسَانُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ
text: and Hell on that day is brought near pulled by seventy thousand sets of reins each set of reins pulled by the hands of seventy thousand angels as it groans and seethes in fury; on that day yawma’idhin is a substitution for idhā ‘when’ the response to which is the following man that is to say the disbeliever will remember his prodigal conduct in it but how will remembering avail him now? the interrogative is meant as a denial in other words his remembering that will not be of any use to him.

arabic: يَقُولُ يٰلَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي
text: He will say as he remembers ‘O yā is for calling attention to something would that I had sent ahead good deeds and faith for my life!’ for a good life in the Hereafter or it means ‘during my life’ in the world.

arabic: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ
text: Then on that day none shall mete out read yu‘adhdhibu His God’s chastisement that is to say He shall not delegate it to any other;

arabic: وَلاَ يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ
text: and likewise none shall bind read yūthiqu His bind a variant reading has yu‘adhdhabu ‘none shall be chastised’ and yūthaqu ‘none shall be bound’ so that the suffixed pronoun of ‘adhābahu and wathāqahu refers to the chastisement and the binds of the disbeliever the meaning then being ‘none shall be chastised as he shall and none shall be bound as he shall be bound’.

arabic: يٰأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ
text: ‘O soul at peace! the one secure namely the believing one.

arabic: ٱرْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً
text: Return — this is said to it upon death — to your Lord that is to say return to His command and to His will pleased with the reward pleasing in God’s sight with your deeds; in other words return O soul combining both descriptions both of which are circumstantial qualifiers. And it will be said to it at the Resurrection

arabic: فَٱدْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي
text: Then enter among My righteous servants!

arabic: وَٱدْخُلِي جَنَّتِي
text: And enter My Paradise!’ with them.

arabic: لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
text: I swear lā is extra by this land of Mecca

arabic: وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ
text: and you O Muhammad (s) have free disposal of sanction for this land in that you will be given permission to fight in it — and indeed God fulfilled this promise to him on the day of the Conquest of Mecca thus this is a parenthetical statement intervening between that by which the oath has been sworn and that which is a supplement thereto.

arabic: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ
text: And by the begetter that is Adam and that which he begat that is his descendants mā ‘that which’ actually means man ‘whom’.

arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ
text: We certainly created man al-insān the generic noun in travail in a state of toil and hardship struggling with the tribulations of this world and the calamities of the Hereafter.

arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ
text: Does he suppose does the strong man of Quraysh namely Abū’l-Ashadd b. Kalada presume on account of his strength that an softened in place of the hardened form its subject omitted that is to say annahu no one will have power over him? Yet God has power over him.

arabic: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً
text: He says ‘I have exhausted in enmity of Muhammad (s) vast wealth!’ great wealth piles and piles of it.

arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ
text: Does he suppose that an in other words annahu no one has seen him? with regard to what he has expended to know the quantity thereof; God knows the quantity thereof; but it is not in reality that much so as to be considered a great amount and in any case He will requite him for his evil conduct.

arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ
text: Have We not given an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We have certainly given’ him two eyes

arabic: وَلِسَاناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ
text: and a tongue and two lips

arabic: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ
text: and guided him to the two paths? did We not point out to him the path of good and that of evil?

arabic: فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ
text: Yet why does he not assault the obstacle? why does he not surmount it?

arabic: وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ
text: And what will show you what will make known to you what the obstacle is? that he is to surmount — intended to emphasise its enormity this statement is a parenthetical one. He explains the way to surmount it by saying

arabic: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ
text: the freeing of a slave from bondage

arabic: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ
text: or to give food on a day of hunger

arabic: يَتِيماً ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ
text: to an orphan near of kin maqraba means qarāba

arabic: أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ
text: or a needy person in misery matraba literally means ‘clinging to the dust turāb’ because of his poverty; a variant reading has two verbal nouns in place of the two verbs fakka ‘he freed’ and at‘ama ‘he fed’ the first being in a genitive construction fakku raqabatin ‘the freeing of a slave’ and the second with nunation it‘āmun ‘to give food’ in which case there is an implied iqtihāmu before al-‘aqaba of which the said reading becomes the explication;

arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِٱلْمَرْحَمَةِ
text: while being thumma kāna is a supplement to iqtahama ‘he assaulted’; thumma is for the ordering of things to be mentioned in other words what is meant is that at the point of the assault he was one of those who believe and enjoin one another to steadfastness in pursuing obedience and in refraining from disobedience and enjoin one another to compassion marhama means rahma towards creatures.

arabic: أُوْلَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ
text: Those the ones described by the said attributes are the ones of the right side al-maymana means al-yamīn.

arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ
text: But those who disbelieve in Our signs they are the ones of the left side al-mash’ama means al-shimāl.

arabic: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
text: Over them will be an enclosing Fire read mu’sada or mūsada closed on top of them.

arabic: وَٱلشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا
text: By the sun and her morning light

arabic: وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلاَهَا
text: and by the moon when it follows her rising after she has set

arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلاَّهَا
text: and by the day when it reveals her as it rises high

arabic: وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا
text: and by the night when it enshrouds her covering her up with its darkness idhā ‘when’ in all three instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath.

arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا
text: By the heaven and the One Who built it

arabic: وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا طَحَاهَا
text: and by the earth and the One Who spread it laid out flat.

arabic: وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا
text: and by the soul that is to say by all souls and the One Who proportioned it in its created form mā in all three instances relates to the verbal action or functions as man ‘the one who’

arabic: فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا
text: and inspired to discern its vices and piety He pointed out to it the path of good and that of evil the placing of taqwā ‘piety’ second takes into account the rhyme endings of the verses; the response to the oath is the following

arabic: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا
text: Successful indeed qad the lām of laqad ‘indeed’ has been omitted from it for the sake of brevity will be the one who purifies it purges it of sins

arabic: وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا
text: and he will indeed have failed he who eclipses it he who obscures it with acts of disobedience dassāhā is actually dassasahā but the second sīn has been replaced with an alif for phonetic ease.

arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَآ
text: Thamūd denied their messenger Sālih because of their rebellious nature

arabic: إِذِ ٱنبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا
text: when the most wretched of them whose name was Qudār was dispatched when he hastened in order to hamstring the she-camel with their approval.

arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا
text: But then the messenger of God Sālih said to them ‘This is the she-camel of God so let her have her drink!’ her drink on her day — one day was hers the next theirs.

arabic: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا
text: But they denied him with regard to his saying this as being a command from God — which if they contravened would immediately result in chastisement being sent down on them — then hamstrung her they slew it in order to appropriate her share of the drinking water. So their Lord closed in on them the chastisement because of their sin and meted it equally among them that is the closing in on them in other words He subsumed them all by it so that not one of them escaped.

arabic: وَلاَ يَخَافُ عُقْبَاهَا
text: And He does not read wa-lā or fa-lā fear the consequence of it.

arabic: وَٱلْلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ
text: By the night as it enshrouds with its darkness all that is between the heaven and the earth

arabic: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
text: and by the day as it unveils as it is revealed and becomes manifest idhā ‘as’ in both instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath

arabic: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلأُنثَىٰ
text: and by the One Who mā either functions as man ‘the One Who’ or it is related to a verbal action created the male and the female Adam and Eve or every male and female — the hermaphrodite although problematic for us is in fact either male or female according to God and therefore a person actually commits perjury if he speaks with one thinking that because he has sworn not to speak with a male or a female; he may do so with a hermaphrodite.

arabic: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ
text: Assuredly your efforts your deeds are dissimilar with some working towards Paradise by means of obedience while others in effect are working towards the Fire through acts of disobedience.

arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
text: As for him who gives what is due to God and is fearful of God

arabic: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
text: and affirms the truth of the best word that is the truth of ‘there is no god but God’ in both places here and below verse 9

arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
text: We shall surely ease his way to the abode of ease to Paradise.

arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
text: But as for him who is niggardly with what is due to God and deems himself self-sufficient without need for His reward 929 and denies the best word

arabic: وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
text: and denies the best word

arabic: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ
text: We shall surely ease his way We shall pave for him the way to hardship to the Fire;

arabic: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ
text: And his wealth shall not mā is or negation avail him when he perishes in the Fire.

arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ
text: Truly with Us lies all guidance the pointing out of the path of guidance from that of error so that Our command may be followed by adhering to the former manner of conduct and that Our prohibition may also be heeded by refraining from falling into the latter manner of conduct.

arabic: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَٱلأُولَىٰ
text: And truly to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life that is to say that of this world and so whoever seeks either of the two from anyone other than Us has erred.

arabic: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَاراً تَلَظَّىٰ
text: So I have warned you of I have threatened you O people of Mecca with a raging fire talazzā ‘raging’ one of the two original tā’ letters of tatalazzā has been omitted; a variant reading retains it tatalazzā that is ‘one that is flaming’

arabic: لاَ يَصْلَٰهَآ إِلاَّ ٱلأَشْقَى
text: which none shall enter but the wretched one al-ashqā means al-shaqī

arabic: ٱلَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
text: he who denies the Prophet and turns away from faith — this delimiting of those who deserve to enter this fire constitutes an interpretation of His saying But He forgives other than that to whomever He will Q. 448 which in turn suggests that what is meant is that entry into the Fire which will be everlasting.

arabic: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَتْقَى
text: The God-fearing one al-atqā means al-taqī shall be spared it he will be removed far away from it

arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ
